# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document expands the phase sequence of
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md) into
> **three levels of tasks that can be committed and verified independently**.
>
> RFC-039 is the sole authority for phase order and acceptance gates; this document is responsible
> only for decomposing the work into an executable granularity and registering conflicts that have
> not yet been adjudicated.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with the phase sequence in RFC-039                                 |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each capable of forming and archiving an independent team |
| **Level 3** | 262         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                             |

**Unused numbers are not recycled**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP
route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). All three have had no
corresponding entries since the WBS was established—the complete history of this document has zero
matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used to verify this),
and the repository as a whole contains no references to them. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1
of `05` (test revival and completion): that phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8’s
numbering remains aligned with its phase number (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale
for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered Level-2/Level-3 row
**must contain two fields**—**Owning Phase** (the P phase to which it truly belongs, which may
differ from its containing section) and **Blocks Mainline?**; `Pending Scheduling` is no longer the
default state, and an unmarked task is deemed **not schedulable**. Numbers **must be unique across
the entire document** (cross-track tasks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not
occupy an `N.x` number).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
present)—written on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching completion items** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. Do **not**
write the fix, the criterion chain, gate values, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a kanban
board, not a process chronicle. Do **not** write decision labels or restatements of conclusions:
“User Decision A/B/C,” “Option A,” “Final implementation is…” and similar text do not belong in this
table—the board answers only “Is it complete?”, while decisions and results can be found in commit
messages and the RFC-039 decision registry.

**Short hashes are authoritative only after the push**: a closure row records the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push is complete. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then
write the closure row** (see [commit-convention](../commit-convention.md), “Obtain the commit number
after push”). The closure commit itself carries no number—a self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains numbers only**: the Level-1/Level-2/Level-3 counts under
`Positioning and Scope` contain only current values; increment/decrement history such as `+1 = …`
does not belong in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” of eight documents into this table, **five hard gaps
in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been closed:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Resolution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no construction steps**. RFC defines P5 (checker split) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how to perform the split; `01-routing.md` contains a single mention of an `annotations.rs` line in its directory tree, the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                                                | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| G2  | **The three ownership assignments for the `include!` refactor resulted in zero implementation**. RFC lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; `06` also lists it under S7. However, `02`’s change list (6 additions + 20 modifications) does **not** contain `semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                                                                                  | The construction steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); references in RFC and 06 have been synchronized to point here                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts**. `RFC` lists 4 `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists 4 scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists another 4 checks (all with different names); `04` previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (this script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` has dual ownership under P4 and P9 | See the unified list in §P9 of this document (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to this table                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum,” and `05` argues for deletion                                                                                                                                                                                       | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registry C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| G5  | **Conflicting statement of the L2 goal**. RFC and the index of this directory describe “grammar-driven syntax,” whereas `05` assesses itself as having **“not adopted true grammar-driven parsing (LALRPOP); [it] only achieved declarative table lookup”**                                                                                                                                                                        | This has converged on **a declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface**: the full LALRPOP grammar-driven route was withdrawn (two attempts produced 29 / 148 conflicts), falling back per 05:648 to “retain Pratt + a single declarative precedence table + cross-checking two `BinOp` implementations against one source”; see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions—do not invent constructs / do not keep filling
indefinitely / do not patch when a refactor is required—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules
must be established before construction begins; otherwise, while reviving tests in P1, work would
already be adding `mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Defects (Minimal Approach)

Source: [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3, defect-fix half ＋ **2026-10-07
silent-drop audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, decision of 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior did not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack overflow, silently giving
> the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactor**, but all four requirements must be
> met: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and must genuinely be red); ② no
> change to the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled successfully
> and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and their existing diagnostic codes/prose/exit
> codes must not be removed or changed); ③ registration in the same commit (this row identifies the
> error type + a revision note for that phase + the PR required block line “Error Type”); ④ baseline
> regeneration in the same commit + manual review of the diff. **D user-visible semantics / E
> external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must still be adjudicated first. For the
> expanded criteria and A–F allowlist, see
> [07 §Semantic-correction routing criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md); the approach of “default
> super-refactor + post-hoc registration” is not adopted** (rationale in RFC-039 D59: a zero-red
> criterion cannot distinguish a fix from a regression and conflicts with “no C5′ exists” and “no
> relaxation of any kind”).

**Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 requires manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 follow C2/C3 and the 9.2 gate in P9. **Risk**: the new
diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavior change and requires synchronized corpus differential baseline and
CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 does not have to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, performance
> baseline) can proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping correctness defects (`Sorted(3)` passing
> silently) must not be blocked by snapshot infrastructure. 3.3 (panic to diagnostic) has no
> prerequisites and can land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint**; it is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (narrowing
Rust’s `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed before P4 as a whole**: 029g’s deletion surface overlaps the rewrite
surfaces of all four refactoring phases; reversing the order means redoing the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the `pub` branch of `collect_exports`       | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→real `mod` and the checker split are **pure moves**, and the `pub` branch would be moved verbatim into the new files)                                                                                                                            |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| The `Public` modifier of `semantic_tokens`                          | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `is_pub`-ignoring binding in `ir_gen`                               | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (`ir_gen.rs` SSA conversion)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase changes them directly, but **P6’s hard acceptance criterion requires zero diff in `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; direct-driver tests under `tests/` are an exception, see the P6 hard-acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Incidental benefit**: 029g deletes the dead `env.exports` table (filled by the producer, with zero
consumers across the repository) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4’s 4.3 obligation
ledger loses one “produced but never consumed” field.

**Acceptance (behavior changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavior changes must first land a red criterion before
   code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced top-level
   bindings in the Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously `pub` items were absolutely
   exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, equivalent new cases must replace
   them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: the diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) require
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG to be
   updated in the same commit; the IR snapshot is expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff
   requires an explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`)⇒ the two must be serial and
cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; implementers may choose which to start first based on the context at hand.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (the P3.5 chapter + the
> main-chain/constraint row) and RFC-039’s D56 were merged into `97071c81b` while cleaning the
> worktree in the parallel stream. That commit’s message records “3.4 supplemental registration +
> D57/D58 decisions documented,” without mentioning this track. History is not rewritten; following
> the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 implementation note), it is
> registered in place as evidence for later bisection.

|                                                  | 4.4.4 SMT shared-solver observation ledger `ConsumerStats`/`CONSUMER_STATS`: every production-path point writes to it, but the production side has zero readers (the only read entry is `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs`). **Decision ① of 2026-10-24: retain it**—write “the sole consumer = tests” as a doc contract (to preserve the observable criterion carrier for D58); decision ②, “delete it,” is not taken (it would require rewriting 4.4.2’s acceptance criterion at the same time, with the rationale in the 4.4 closure item “sixteen”). **Final state**: the three contract sentences are written into the module header of `src/frontend/core/typecheck/proof/smt/backend.rs` and the relevant item documentation—① the write surface = one atomic increment for each acquisition through the shared entry; ② the read surface is **only** `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs` (zero calls from production code); ③ `SolverConsumer::ALL` is a **test-only constant**, and production code must not depend on it; **zero behavior change** (the changed surface consists only of comments, and 4.4.2’s acceptance number is unchanged; issue [#475](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/475)) |                                                  | 4.9.9 Cross-unit single-definition methods lose the formal-name table when called with named arguments (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closure period): calling a cross-unit method (injected through the registry) with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, and named-argument calls within a single file work normally. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Type C (primary fix) + Type D list (conflicting forms are always rejected, pending user decision)** (the old behavior was not success: the old named-argument path silently dropped arguments and then failed at runtime or silently produced the wrong value; the positional path does not consume the name table, but under **name-level ambiguity** (the same-named type is provided by ≥2 modules), it belongs to another criterion: when the host module and candidate-provider module have the same source, admission is allowed; when they have different sources but the two candidate signatures are identical, admission is allowed; conflicting forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers) always produce E1107 for positional arguments (see ④ below). The mechanism is a **consumer-side key mismatch**—the IR-generation-side formal-name query has only three sources: the current unit’s `fn_param_names` / leaf names / module export surface; the first segment of the method key `{Type}.{method}` is a type name rather than a module key and therefore never hits the export surface). **Root cause and fix (single point, without introducing a second name table)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::lookup_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`) gains the source `method_param_info`—retrieve the formal-name table from the existing sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (candidate ↔ mixed name ↔ formal names are three parallel vectors; `extract_module_info` ← `method_overload_snapshot`, the same source as the typecheck injection surface) using the key `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]`, and the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses `method_dispatch_name`’s defining-unit qualified name as the query key; ② the candidate injection surface’s narrowing rule pairs by target (definition-side type name), while candidates imported through aliases continue to be injected; ③ **provider priority** (the bare-name provider `local == target` has priority, and aliases fill in only when the bare name is absent; same-level multiple modules with the same full name are skipped) is now the **shared single point** `frontend::module::import_face::TypeCandidateProviders`—the injection surface (`driver::arms.rs`) and the consumer side (`middle::lower::query`) read the same source and no longer evolve independently; ④ the **same-source criterion** (`method_source_mismatch`, `src/middle/lower/query.rs`): let `winner` = the providing module selected by the candidate injection surface and `owner` = the module to which the receiver belongs (the same ownership determination as `method_dispatch_name`)—`owner == winner` ⇒ admit (typecheck and IR use candidates from the same module; the bare-name positional case belongs here, measured 2.0 + 2.0 = 4.0); `owner != winner` ⇒ admit only when the two modules have **exactly identical candidate signatures** for the key (candidate selection does not affect type checking, and the value is determined by the receiver’s owning unit—the existing behavior for cross-unit same-named types introduced through inline aliases), otherwise reject loudly (the existing E1107). **Positional arguments with identical signatures are still admitted** (4.9.8 fixture 0/0; the value is determined by the receiver’s unit). Conflicting forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers, the injection surface skipping the full name) take the **conflict branch**: named arguments produce E1014; positional arguments **always produce E1107**—irrespective of argument type, arity, or which side owns the receiver; the determination depends only on the import surface, so the same input has a deterministic result. The IR no longer duplicates typecheck’s type-compatibility rules (the previous narrow compatibility criterion has been deleted); the deterministic companion is that `all_method_bindings` merges in ascending module-key order instead of randomly overwriting according to HashMap iteration order. **Type D list (pending user decision)**: forms in the conflict category that were usable before t5 now always produce E1107, and are registered by “category + representative example” in the 4.9.10 row; Type C cases (old behavior for differing formal types was nondeterministic, mismatched arity silently produced a wrong value, and named arguments failed at runtime) are listed separately and not mixed with Type D. **Named arguments** under name-level ambiguity (the same-named type is provided by ≥2 modules) are still always rejected loudly (the shared criterion’s empty-table exit = the existing E1014): the name table is untrustworthy and cannot be checked by name; ⑤ the **fallback for “do not silently discard named arguments”**: `reject_named_args_without_param_names` reuses the empty-table exit of the shared criterion `arg_binding::bind_args_to_params` (the existing E1014, with `available` using the same semantics = an empty string), and is connected to the IR-side’s four arms with named arguments but no formal-name table—the RFC-004 binding arm, namespace arm, ordinary-method arm without overload resolution, and ordinary **static**-function arm; the built-in container-constructor arm (`src/middle/lower/expr/container.rs`) likewise rejects named arguments other than `len`; ⑥ the **fallback exclusion surface is determined by binding identity**: closure-value bindings (`stmt.rs`’s `closure_fn_names`: the bound value is written as an `=>` lambda and the declaration has no value parameters), current-unit top-level function bindings (`declared_fn_names`), and **named nested function declarations** (`nested_functions` entries) do **not** enter the fallback—all three had the old behavior of “compilation succeeds and named arguments are ignored,” and changing that to a compile-time error is D59 Type D; all three are registered together as known gaps (D60 ② “should report but does not,” Type A). **Visible changes (list each one; do not merge them into “no behavior change”)**: ① cross-unit method named arguments (bare import / alias import / two overload candidates) change from an E1014 empty table → binding by name into slots (measured 6.0 / 30); ② aliased imports (single provider) with named method arguments change from silent argument dropping (runtime `E6007`) → binding by name into slots (6.0); ③ the g9g generic curried method with named arguments changes from silent argument dropping (`b.v` reads Void, runtime `E6007 Void vs Int`) → compile-time E1014 (Type C); ④ cross-unit ordinary function named arguments silently dropped → E1014 (Type C); ⑤ const generic receiver methods with named arguments silently dropped → E1014 (Type C; the **positional** form of the same shape still fails, an existing independent defect outside this task); ⑥ built-in container construction `Vec(Int)(foo = 3)` silently ignored → E1014 (Type C; `Vec(Int)(len = 3)` still gives 0/0 and has the value assertion `v.length == 3`); ⑦ whole-module imports (`use lib` + `lib.Circle(...)`) with named arguments silently dropped → E1014 (Type C); ⑧ named arguments on **name-level ambiguous** types always produce E1014; positional arguments: `owner == winner` and “`owner != winner` but candidate signatures are identical” are admitted (value assertions 4.0 / 200 / 20); different sources with differing signatures, or conflicting forms, always produce E1107 (three measured cases of silent wrong values eliminated: differing formal types, differing arity, and differing return type; the conflict-form cost list is in 4.9.10); ⑨ named arguments on closure-value bindings (top-level `f = () => 7` and function-body forms), block-body function declarations (`f: (a: Int) -> Int = { 7 }`), and named nested function declarations (body ignores formal parameters) **retain the old behavior** (named arguments ignored, measured result 7), with no judgment change. **Residual / known gaps**: named arguments on the three declaration surfaces above are still silently ignored (Type A, D60 ② “should report but does not”); the formal-name table of named nested functions is not yet connected to `lookup_param_info`; the E1014 prose is limited: an empty `available` means “the IR did not obtain a name table,” not “the function truly has no such parameter,” and this task neither changes the prose nor expands the diagnostic surface; the same-source criterion’s signature comparison is structural equivalence (it does not compare implementations), and the residual risk of “identical signatures, different implementations” is covered in 4.9.10. **Criterion**: 30 driver-level direct tests in method-candidate key `{Type}.{method}` contains no module qualification, so for same-named types across modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`arms.rs::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck’s formal-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—**each guesses the provider by name**, and changing any one of them merely moves the “silently wrong value” elsewhere. 4.9.9’s stop-the-bleeding criterion is: under name-level ambiguity, named arguments always produce E1014; positional arguments—same source (candidate provider module == receiver’s owning module) are admitted, differing sources with identical candidate signatures are admitted, and **conflicting forms (name-level ambiguity, ≥2 providers) always produce E1107** (the IR does not duplicate typecheck’s compatibility rules); the root fix = upgrade the method key to a **module-qualified identity**, resolve it in one place, and have all three consumers read it, requiring changes to the `overload_resolutions` key shape and mixed name (D59 **Type D**, requires a decision) Root fix = module-qualified method key (this task), after which full type checking against the receiver owner’s candidates is performed and Type D usability can be restored. |

### P5 In-File Checker Split — Supplemented by This Document (Original Gap G1)

Source: RFC definition + the directory tree in `01-routing.md` + hard constraint (the `pub(crate)`
path of `collect_used_in_type` must not change)

- [x] **5.1 `include!` → real `mod`** (2 Level-3 tasks)
- [x] **5.2 Extract `refinement`** (2 Level-3 tasks)
- [x] **5.3 Extract `annotations`** (2 Level-3 tasks)

| Level 2                     | Level 3                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Prerequisite | Acceptance                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 5.1 `include!` → real `mod` | 5.1.1 Change the `include!` at the end of `checker.rs` to a real `mod` declaration (do not hard-code a line anchor; it was measured at the end of the file at the time)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | P4 complete  | C1 zero-diff; `semantic_tokens.rs` gains module identity                                                                                    |
|                             | 5.1.2 Add `use super::*` or import items individually (scope was inherited implicitly in the `include!` era)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | 5.1.1        | `cargo build` is green                                                                                                                      |
| 5.2 Extract `refinement`    | 5.2.1 Move the refinement blocks out (the three noncontiguous ranges formerly in `checker.rs`; now one `checker/refinement.rs` file containing `ReturnRefinement` / `RefinedWalkCtx`), leaving the retained surface and 6 cross-boundary shared items in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | 5.1.1        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                |
|                             | 5.2.2 Converge the refinement entry point on “`&self` + return diagnostics” and **do not leave the impl**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer implicitly writes to the error channel through `&mut self`; the diagnostic set is returned upward, and its single write site is the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Reason for not leaving the impl**: the only field used by this family is `self.env` (so technically leaving the impl would be feasible), but “convert both the entry point and the walk to free functions” would also move these call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 production sites (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), and `collect_param_refinements` has 2 production sites + 1 test site, while creating a reverse dependency from the “retained surface (signature collection) → refinement”—the opposite of the coupling this step is intended to eliminate | 5.2.1        | —                                                                                                                                           |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move out the 10-item annotation-validation family (now one `checker/annotations.rs` file; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a family-local free function)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 5.2.2        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                |
|                             | 5.3.2 **`collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) remains `pub(crate)` and remains under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 **did not migrate it** according to measurement ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` as a re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is migrated with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` as a re-export so that the existing import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 5.3.1        | **“Zero caller changes” is this step’s hard acceptance criterion**: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is migrated with the annotation family in the future, `checker.rs` **must then**
add `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` as a re-export so that the import remains unchanged;
measurement shows that 5.3 **did not migrate it**, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion
was already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of only 200–400 lines—this adds
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are deferred until the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: the end state of D62 is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions
> share the same compile-time items. A strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> implementation-head binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equivalence is a **pure
> decision** (both sides normalize to the same value; it does not bind type variables); evidence is
> the **sole entry** for q=0 slots (literal/value environment/single-value pinning/Γ equality, four
> sources); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (it holds for closed terms and open
> terms/recursion); Σ construction points **reuse** the same evidence interface rather than creating
> another one. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that substage names have been
> completed.**

> **6.9 closure criterion**: I1–I5 and I7 all hold, I6 is closed according to the design-review
> conclusion for 6.9.5 (does not block P7), and I8 has evidence for every slice; residual items
> #537/#539/#540/#541/#542/#552 all have dispositions (fixed/explicitly excluded/separate case);
> #542 landed on 2026-11-19. **Do not substitute “all substages checked” for the invariants
> holding.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A facts → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B kernel → {B.d,
> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 decision → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d can run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans toward typecheck→mono, d toward types/solver→sema), and C.2
> can run in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not depend on defeq); D’s
> implementation waits for confirmation of the B design package; it depends on A (q=0 erasure) and
> C.1 (dispatch), and may depend on the 6.9.3 typed exit. **P7 gate = A/B/C exits; D does not
> block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 decision (decided as A on 2026-11-16; measured)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is
> created, and the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already carry `k-1`.
> **The decision has changed to two orthogonal decisions plus one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open term enters `deferred` and is normalized before enqueueing / B: no
> specialization); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1’s second field and C-2 reconstruction from
> IR both break the single representation/evaluator, so C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive firing
> drives the recursive chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a: fold the condition within the
> instance / T-b: bounded firing + return to the original at the boundary / T-c: termination layer
> or amend the specification). **Implement first, then decide; before measurement, “A is
> implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16): D-a=A-close, D-b=C-3,
> F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task, and complete I4 is not claimed.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that “a
> decision point first follows the unified path; after unified failure, it may use equivalence, but
> must first roll back the partial bindings produced by the unified attempt.” The implementation
> must answer: is the entry an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new `decide` layer; may
> defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (no unbound variables); what are the
> snapshot/restoration boundaries and costs; and do unify and defeq share one budget or have one
> each. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for subtyping/Any/Never; defeq only
> determines equivalence and does not take over subtyping; bidirectional subtyping must not be
> treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol and production call graph before
> writing code**; the 6.9.3c wiring contract was already wasted on two rounds by assuming
> `can_assign` was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or a line-by-line classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ idempotence of the error-code generator (if an emission point/code table
> changes); and ④ classification of behavior changes under D59, with red before green. **Wiring
> tasks additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (the production entry, number of
> paths, and which path is reachable); unit-test reachability must not be passed off as user
> reachability; rollback and budget must have measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537 (Type
> D, proof-function formal refinement is silently discarded; do not fix before the decision, and
> 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; a C-stage boundary; if it
> remains open, 6.9.4 covers only module-local forms), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow;
> **closed**—3.20.30 was closed on 2026-11-14: a 64MB large-stack thread in the orchestration
> layer + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see row 3.20.30 in 09), #541 (TailCall;
> **closed**—on 2026-11-16, three sites moved in and out together: `call_form_is_rewritten` /
> `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` cover `Call`/`TailCall` through the single
> `rewritten_call_target` point; the init section and function bodies share one site-rewriting
> source; red→green + three mutations), #542 (isolated shared layer; **implemented (2026-11-19)**:
> DCE pass + post-mono two-entry wiring + C2c temporary workaround removal; red→green, 402/402,
> function-table attribution and deviations), and #552 (imported multi-parameter predicate proof
> execution; adjacent to 6.9.5, separate case). **Ownership pending decision**: the four
> open-constraint tripwires in `rfc027_refined_transparency` (`Eq(N, n)`) do not belong to 6.9.4’s
> constant-equality bridge; leave them in 6.9.4 outOfScope or move them to 6.9.1/E4018’s
> proof-function surface, subject to a decision.

> **Non-claims / boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim complete Π/Σ; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and does not
> fulfill the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; the second value position of `f(y)(y)` is outside
> this item; witness erasure ≠ Runtime check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5 cover only

`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-driver test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive changed code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified **when mechanically required**, but every
modification must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted and
assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new
diagnostic codes + baseline updates), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round requiring a separate decision.

> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying zero-diff to the entire `tests/` directory; the

> **corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The remainder of P2 (2.1
> IR verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) can proceed
> in parallel with P3. Stopping correctness defects is not blocked by criterion infrastructure;
> however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver requires all three layers of
> criteria to be in place.

| Constraint         | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1            | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P1 → P2            | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| P2 (narrowed) → P3 | Defect criteria must be **written red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P3 → P4            | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to become entrenched as “existing behavior” in the stage table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| P3.5 → P4          | RFC-029g (#399)’s deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| P4 → P5            | The `include!` refactor and checker split touch the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| P5 → P6            | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P6 → P7 / P8       | Type representations must converge first, or the new IR will grow into a third representation; **the P7 gate = the stage A/B/C exits of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and 6.9.4 complete), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface and must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume the undecided defeq/quantifier interface |
| P7/P8 → P9         | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and 9.3’s `pub(crate)` leak count can take their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | The file sets are disjoint: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs. `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod` and is individually revertible                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly states under S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are independent after 4.1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 can be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | The file sets are disjoint (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 touches `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 touches `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 touches two `pub` locations in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; there are no pairwise intersections) |

**Non-parallelizable (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (the same
batch file for B6/E5); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s `pub` deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serial).

**Additional internal document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move prerequisite batch for P7), and 7b’s `Phi` arm
must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “pre-hoc judgments.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was required”; only the
  D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the three coexisting lists in the original G3
  gap made closure impossible. This table merges them so that 10 active scripts each belong to one
  phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and hard-gate
  transition points explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to do after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactor means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status corrections into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplemented by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the
  largest single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the granularity at which the
  work can be rolled back.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it says only that “fixed defects
  must not be rolled back,” and lacks a requirement to record “what was fixed.” **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description as evidence for later bisection.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b, two exclusive
  commits, per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse**—approximately 89 reference renames; missing one will **silently change
  associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 lands as 7e.1,
  D20 lands as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation is incorporated into 7e.1, with deletion
  actions left in P10 S6.
- ~~**The 2315 / 2341 data-loss defects were originally “separate issues”**~~ **Fixed
  (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core language
  semantics and must not be left as an unimplemented legacy item.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as
  the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.
